extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of sociology, economic theory, and social evolution (readers of Veblen)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and summarizing Veblen's criteria and distinctions about human temperament, occupational selection, and the formation/selection of the leisure class—especially the contrasts between predatory/pecuniary and peaceable/industrial dispositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human nature variants: predatory vs peaceable
rubrics_metrics.description: Human nature is presented as variants: an earlier 'peaceable, savage' ante-predatory type and a later 'predatory' (barbarian/pecuniary) variant; modern individuals tend to breed true to the recent predatory/quasi-peaceable hereditary present but may revert to the ante-predatory variant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Veblen uses these variants to explain tendencies of temperament, reversion under changed circumstances, and the mixed heredity of Occidental populations; terms are used somewhat loosely and may overlap with ethnic-type variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predatory-barbarian temperament traits
rubrics_metrics.description: The predatory or barbarian temperament is characterised by ferocity, self-seeking, clannishness, disingenuousness, and a free resort to force and fraud; an unremitting emulation and antagonism between classes and individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These traits are those best fitted to survive under a 'regime of status' or pecuniary culture; selection under prolonged predatory discipline tends to accentuate them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peaceable (ante-predatory) temperament traits
rubrics_metrics.description: Traits surviving from the earlier peaceable phase include an instinct of race solidarity (conscience), truthfulness and equity, the instinct of workmanship in a naive non-invidious form, peaceableness, good-will, and a non-invidious interest in men and things; also characteristic shortcomings such as weakness, inefficiency, lack of initiative, and indolent amiability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These traits are useful for collective life and persist as hereditary habits but are liable to repression under competitive predatory conditions; they reassert when pressures of predatory exigency are relieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traits required for success of a modern industrial community (collective interest)
rubrics_metrics.description: The collective interest of the modern industrial community is best served by honesty, diligence, peacefulness, good-will, an absence of self-seeking, and a habitual recognition and apprehension of causal sequence (without animistic belief).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The complex, organized mechanism of industrial life works best when these traits concur; they are less present in the predatory type and are the aptitudes industrial society tends to favor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traits promoting individual success under pecuniary/competitive regime
rubrics_metrics.description: Under competitive pecuniary conditions the individual's immediate interest is best furthered by freedom from scruple, lack of sympathy, unscrupulous conversion of goods and persons to one's ends, a keen sense of status, shrewd trading, and unscrupulous management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These traits advantage the individual in pecuniary emulation even though they may be disserviceable to collective industrial ends; highly successful men historically often display these traits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of employments: pecuniary vs industrial
rubrics_metrics.description: Employments are divided into pecuniary (ownership, acquisition, financiering, mercantile) and industrial (workmanship, production); the two differ materially in aptitudes required and the formative training they give.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinction explains divergent educative and selective actions of economic life: pecuniary employments conserve predatory aptitudes, industrial employments foster workmanship and non-invidious habits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reputability hierarchy of employments
rubrics_metrics.description: A hierarchy of respectability attaches to employments: large-scale ownership and financiering are most reputable; banking and the law rank high; mercantile pursuits vary; manual labor and factory labor are low in conventional respectability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reputability reinforces leisure-class standards and sustains the prestige of predatory aptitudes; perceived usefulness and association with ownership influence rank.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pecuniary employments conserve predatory aptitudes
rubrics_metrics.description: The discipline of pecuniary employments conserves and cultivates predatory habits (chicanery, shrewdness) by educating participants and selectively repressing or eliminating lines unfit for pecuniary competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include ownership, financiering, and much mercantile activity; as business scales grow, some routine aspects moderate the immediate suggestion of overreaching for subordinates, but ownership/administration remain tied to predatory disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial employments cultivate workmanship and non-invidious aptitudes
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial occupations, concerned with the apprehension and coordination of mechanical facts and sequences, educate and select for non-invidious habits of thought and hasten the obsolescence of distinctively predatory aptitudes among workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although industrial workers are also affected by pecuniary concerns (wages, purchase of goods), their primary training adapts them to collective, non-emulative purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leisure class admission criterion: pecuniary aptitude
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrance to the leisure class lies through pecuniary employments: those admitted have been pecuniarily successful and therefore presumed to possess an above-average complement of predatory/pecuniary aptitudes; nouveaux arrivés are a 'picked body'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection continually withdraws those eminently fitted for aggressive pecuniary competition from lower classes; reversionary non-predatory tendencies among the upper class are commonly weeded out if they threaten pecuniary standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical shift in selection grounds for leisure class
rubrics_metrics.description: The criteria for admission have changed historically: early barbarian stages tested prowess (clannishness, ferocity, massiveness); later quasi-peaceable regimes favored shrewd practice, prudence, providence, and chicanery; the modern trend favors pecuniary aptitudes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This historical change explains why the leisure-class character evolves: what counts as 'fitness' shifts with the dominant mode of acquisition and tenure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenacity of purpose as a broadly selected trait
rubrics_metrics.description: Tenacity of purpose or consistency of aim is a trait conserved across different classes (both pecuniary and industrial) and distinguishes them from the shiftless dependent or the delinquent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While tenacity is not uniquely pecuniary, it differentiates successful persons from those unable to sustain productive or acquisitive effort; it may be selected by both industrial and pecuniary processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two divergent lines of selective development: capacities and propensities
rubrics_metrics.description: Veblen identifies two main divergent axes of selective development: (1) capacities — the pecuniary vs the industrial line (skills and aptitudes conserved in individuals), and (2) propensities or animus — the invidious (self-regarding) vs the non-invidious (economical).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The overall objective point of evolution is not singular; selection tends toward greater stability of aim and persistence in effort, but important minor tendencies diverge along these two lines.
